items.title: Berkshire Now Holds 10% of Lennar. What’s Keeping It From Buying All of the Home Builder.
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway  purchased more than $200 million of depressed  Lennar  stock over three trading days and now owns just over 10% of the country’s second largest home builder.  Berkshire bought about 2.6 million shares of Lennar’s Class A shares on Thursday, Friday, and Monday.  The company also owns over 500,000 shares of Lennar’s supervoting Class B stock.

items.title: LEN Stock Rises Overnight As Berkshire Picks $212M Lot Amid Housing Weakness
items.summary: Warren Buffett’s conglomerate expands its position in the U.S. homebuilder.

items.title: Is Lennar Stock Really On Sale?
items.summary: Lennar (LEN) stock sits near $76, its 52-week low, after losing about 39% over the past year while the S&P 500 gained 17% with dividends reinvested. That is below its book value of roughly $91 a share at the end of fiscal Q3 2026, and the CEO says the stock is on sale. The easy read is a bargain. The catch is land that Lennar agreed to buy in very different market conditions, and part of that bill still has no number on it.

items.title: Why Lennar Is Getting Hit Worse Than D.R. Horton in This Crummy Housing Market
items.summary: Lennar, the nation’s third-largest home builder, had a earnings miss last week. But it wasn’t inflation driving up construction materials or tariffs or wages or any of the other usual suspects that stood out. It was land holdings.

items.title: What Happens To Lennar Stock If Its Home Sales Keep Slowing?
items.summary: Lennar (LEN) stock has lost about 41% over the past year, and on September 18 it closed at the bottom of its 52-week range. The bigger risk sits inside the business. Its plan to rebuild profit depends on selling homes at a steady pace, and its own numbers show that pace slipping.
